headline: Day Use and Campground Registration in Kluane
reservation: Kathleen Lake operates on a first-come, first-served basis for its campground, though backcountry permits for the Cottonwood Trail require advance registration. Always check the Parks Canada Kluane website for updated campfire bans and site availability before arriving from Whitehorse.

days.title: Alpine Ridges and Lakeshore Paths

stops.name: King's Throne Trail
stops.detail: Ascend the glacial cirque for panoramic views of the lake's turquoise waters and the Shakwak Valley.

stops.name: Kathleen Lake Day Use Area
stops.detail: Walk the boardwalk to view the unique 'kokanee' salmon habitat and the dramatic mountain reflections.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes from Haines Junction; conditions vary by wind.
days.note: The King's Throne trail is steep and exposed; check wind speeds at the visitor center.

days.title: Cottonwood Vistas and Wilderness Transitions
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Kathleen Lake Campground

stops.name: Cottonwood Trailhead
stops.detail: Begin a section of this multi-day loop to experience the transition from boreal forest to alpine meadows.

stops.name: Mush Lake Road
stops.detail: Explore the periphery of the park boundary where grizzly sightings are frequent in the berry season.

days.driving: Local driving between trailheads; roads are gravel and may be narrow.
days.note: Bear spray and proper storage are mandatory due to high grizzly density in this corridor.

days.title: Glacial History and Departure

stops.name: Da Kų Cultural Centre
stops.detail: Visit this nearby Haines Junction landmark to understand the Champagne and Aishihik First Nations' connection to the land.

stops.name: Rock Glacier Trail
stops.detail: Observe the unique geological formation of a glacier covered in rock debris just south of the lake.

days.driving: Allow 2.5 hours for the return trip to Whitehorse.
days.note: Fuel is available in Haines Junction; ensure tanks are full before heading south toward the lake.

intel.title: Day Use Capacity
intel.text: The main lot near the boat launch serves both hikers and paddlers. It can become congested on sunny weekends in July, so early arrival is recommended.

intel.title: Highway Coverage
intel.text: Cell reception is reliable in Haines Junction but drops significantly as you approach the Kathleen Lake valley. Download maps for offline use before leaving town.

intel.title: Haines Junction Services
intel.text: This is the primary service hub for the area. Ensure you have supplies here, as there are no services at the lake itself.

intel.title: Wind and Water
intel.text: Kathleen Lake is notorious for sudden, high-velocity winds that make paddling dangerous. Check the flag warnings at the boat launch before launching.

intel.title: Seasonal Gate Closure
intel.text: The main road to the lake is maintained in summer, but winter access may require snowshoes or skis from the highway gate. Check seasonal dates locally.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental in Whitehorse and stock up on groceries before the two-hour drive to Haines Junction for park orientation.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for the paved access road; high-clearance is better for the Mush Lake area.
plan.goldenHour: The King's Throne cirque glows during the long summer twilight, visible from the lakeshore boardwalk.
